block.title: Low glide over still water at first light, fortress reflection dissolving
block.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering, bold dark outlines, saturated limited palette, widescreen arcade composition, subtle CRT scanline glow; ending scene painted at hi-resolution, intimate scale, ultra-detailed large-format art with pixel-art texture accents. Seconds from landing: a battered steel-blue dart fighter — one engine flare dimmer than the other, canopy cracked in a fine star, hull stripe scorched along its flank — skims just meters above a vast wind-stilled sea at first light, its underside mirrored almost perfectly in the dark water. The sky is a gradient wall of pale gold breaking through low rose cloud, the sun a thin new half-arc resting on the far horizon rim, and that gold lays one long trembling road of light across the water straight toward the ship. Behind, on the far horizon, the great fortress of the enemy is dying honestly: a low silhouette of broken citadel spires wreathed in slow columnless haze, its mass already half-sunk into the morning, and in the water its reflection is coming apart — the mirrored towers broken into soft drifting bands of dark ripple, as if the sea were erasing the memory faster than the eye can hold it. Spray stirs in two tiny fans at the wingtips where the hull kisses the air above the water. Everything in this frame is quiet and slightly bruised and entirely alive. Palette of pale gold dawn over deep teal-navy water with rose cloud rims, lifted deep-navy shadows, never pure black. No text, no letters, no UI.

The dissolving fortress-reflection is the poetic core; if the model mirrors it too cleanly, add "reflection visibly rippling apart."
